_comment: Lip colour families, not products. Each entry is a colour with a common
descriptive name and the undertone it flatters — a colour-theory claim,
not a claim that any particular product exists in this shade. Product
lookup is a separate concern (see data/shades.json and issue #7).
undertone_affinity: which skin undertone the family sits well against.
depth_range: Monk levels where the family reads as intended rather than
disappearing (too light on deep skin) or overwhelming (too dark on fair).
Ranges overlap on purpose; these are soft preferences, not rules.

families.name: Soft rose
families.note: Blue-based pink; keeps fair cool skin from looking washed out.

families.name: Mauve
families.note: Muted pink-purple; the everyday neutral for cool undertones.

families.name: Berry
families.note: Deep blue-red; high contrast without going black.

families.name: Plum
families.note: Reads rich rather than heavy on deeper cool skin.

families.name: Blue-red
families.note: The classic red that suits cool undertones; makes teeth look whiter.

families.name: Peach
families.note: Golden coral; echoes the yellow in warm fair skin.

families.name: Terracotta
families.note: Earthy orange-brown; the warm equivalent of a nude.

families.name: Brick
families.note: Orange-red; warmer and softer than a true red.

families.name: Copper
families.note: Metallic-leaning warm brown; strong on deeper warm skin.

families.name: Warm caramel
families.note: Deep golden brown; a daytime neutral at depth.

families.name: Rosewood
families.note: Balanced pink-brown; the safest everyday shade.

families.name: True red
families.note: Neither blue nor orange; the red that works on most people.

families.name: Chestnut
families.note: Neutral brown; the deep-skin counterpart to a nude.

families.name: Wine
families.note: Deep neutral red; dramatic but not costume.

families.name: Nude beige
families.note: Only reads as nude on fair skin; muddy past MST 5.
